title: Subdivision 118-B — main residence CGT exemption
summary: A capital gain or loss from a CGT event happening to a dwelling (or ownership interest in it) is disregarded if the dwelling was your main residence throughout your ownership period (s 118-110). The exemption is modified by rules that extend it (moving in, changing residences, absences up to 6 years, building/renovating, destruction and replacement) and rules that limit it (partial exemption for periods of non-main-residence use under s 118-185, income-producing use under s 118-190, first use to produce income under s 118-192, and the foreign-resident boundary). Deceased estates have their own exemption (s 118-195) and partial exemption (s 118-200) with adjustments for multiple inheritances (s 118-205). Trustee provisions (s 118-210), special disability trusts (ss 118-215 to 118-230), and spouse-transfer interactions (ss 118-178, 118-180 via Subdiv 126-A roll-over) are also mapped. The foreign-resident boundary at s 118-110(3)-(5): 'excluded foreign resident' (>6 years continuous foreign residency) or foreign resident failing the 'life events test' cannot claim the exemption. Covers ss 118-105 to 118-265. Subsection coverage: operative 118-105, 118-110(1)-(5), 118-115(1)-(2), 118-120(1)-(6), 118-125, 118-130(1)-(3), 118-135, 118-140(1)-(2), 118-145(1)-(4), 118-147(1)-(7), 118-150(1)-(6), 118-155(1)-(5), 118-160(1)-(3), 118-165, 118-170(1)-(4), 118-175, 118-178(1)-(2), 118-180(1)-(2), 118-185(1)-(3), 118-190(1)-(4), 118-192(1)-(3), 118-195(1)-(2), 118-197, 118-200(1)-(4), 118-205(1)-(4), 118-210(1)-(6), 118-220, 118-222, 118-225(1)-(5), 118-227(1)-(3), 118-230, 118-240, 118-245(1)-(3), 118-250(1)-(4), 118-255, 118-260(1)-(2), 118-265 mapped; 118-137, 118-149, 118-198, 118-211, 118-212 (not present in compilation 263); 118-215 (guide only).

nodes.label: A CGT event happens to your dwelling (or ownership interest in it)
nodes.body: Subdivision 118-B provides an exemption from CGT for a dwelling that was your main residence (s 118-105). The exemption disregards the capital gain or loss. Only specified CGT events qualify: A1, B1, C1, C2, E1, E2, F2, K3, K4, K6 (and forfeited deposits in an uninterrupted transaction sequence leading to one of these) — s 118-110(2).

nodes.label: Is the CGT event one that qualifies for the main residence exemption?
nodes.body: Only CGT events A1, B1, C1, C2, E1, E2, F2, K3, K4 and K6 qualify (s 118-110(2)(a)). Also qualify: a CGT event involving forfeiting a deposit as part of an uninterrupted sequence ending in one of those events (s 118-110(2)(b)). CGT events not listed are outside the scope of this Subdivision.

nodes.label: Are you an individual?
nodes.body: s 118-110(1)(a): the BASIC case requires you to be an individual. But the deceased-estate rules (ss 118-195, 118-200, 118-210) and special disability trust rules (ss 118-215 to 118-230) extend the exemption to trustees and beneficiaries — a non-individual can still claim through those regimes. Non-individuals are routed to the deceased-estate/special-disability-trust checks, not straight to no-exemption.

nodes.label: Is the CGT asset a dwelling (including adjacent land/structures)?
nodes.body: 'Dwelling' includes a building or unit of accommodation consisting wholly or mainly of residential accommodation, a caravan, houseboat or other mobile home, and any land immediately under it (s 118-115(1)). Adjacent land used primarily for private/domestic purposes in association with the dwelling is treated as part of the dwelling, up to a maximum of 2 hectares less the area under the dwelling (s 118-120(1)-(3)). Adjacent structures (garage, storeroom) associated with a flat or home unit are also included (s 118-120(5)-(6)).

nodes.label: Do you have an ownership interest in the dwelling?
nodes.body: You have an ownership interest if you have a legal or equitable interest in the land, a right to occupy it, a licence, a stratum unit interest in a flat/home unit, or a share in a company that owns the land and gives you a right to occupy (s 118-130(1)). For contract acquisitions, the interest runs from legal ownership or an earlier contractual right to occupy (s 118-130(2)). The ownership period (s 118-125) is the period on or after 20 September 1985 when you had the interest.

nodes.label: Are you a foreign resident blocked by s 118-110(3)-(5)?
nodes.body: s 118-110(3): the basic case does NOT apply if at the time of the CGT event you are (a) an EXCLUDED foreign resident — foreign resident for a continuous period of more than 6 years ending at that time (s 118-110(4)); or (b) a foreign resident who does not satisfy the LIFE EVENTS TEST (s 118-110(5)): foreign resident for 6 years or less AND (i) you or your spouse had a terminal medical condition during that period; (ii) your child (under 18 at the time) had a terminal medical condition during the period; (iii) your spouse, or your child who was under 18 at death, died during that period; or (iv) the CGT event happens because of a s 126-5(1) matter involving you and your spouse/former spouse. There is NO acquisition-date test in the section itself.

nodes.label: No exemption — foreign resident blocked (s 118-110(3)-(5))
nodes.body: If you are an excluded foreign resident (>6 years continuous foreign residency) or a foreign resident who does not satisfy the life events test, the main residence exemption under s 118-110 does not apply. The partial exemption under s 118-185 is also blocked (s 118-185(3)). The dwelling is treated as if it were not your main residence for CGT purposes. The capital gain from the CGT event is assessable under the normal CGT rules. The foreign resident may still consider Div 855 (foreign resident CGT) — see the Div 855 map — and the s 855-10 disregard if the dwelling is not taxable Australian property.

nodes.label: Was the dwelling your main residence throughout your ownership period?
nodes.body: For the full exemption to apply under the basic case (s 118-110(1)(b)), the dwelling must have been your main residence for the entire ownership period. If it was your main residence only for part of the period, you may still get a partial exemption under s 118-185. The extension rules (ss 118-135 to 118-160) may treat the dwelling as having been your main residence for periods when it technically was not — including moving-in grace periods, absences up to 6 years, building/renovating time, and changing-residence overlap periods.

nodes.body: Even if the dwelling was not physically your main residence throughout the ownership period, the following rules may extend the exemption by treating it as your main residence for certain periods: s 118-135 (moving into a dwelling — grace period until it is first practicable to move in); s 118-140 (changing main residences — 6-month overlap); s 118-145 (absences — 6-year absence rule with choice); s 118-147 (absence from replacement dwelling after compulsory acquisition/destruction); s 118-150 (building/repairing/renovating — up to 4 years); s 118-155 (death during building); s 118-160 (destruction of dwelling and sale of land).

nodes.label: Do you choose to treat the dwelling as your main residence during a period of absence (s 118-145)?
nodes.body: If you move out of a dwelling that was your main residence, you may choose to continue treating it as your main residence (s 118-145(1)). If any part was used to produce assessable income, the maximum continuous period is 6 years (s 118-145(2) — another 6-year period starts each time it re-becomes your main residence). If not used for income, the period is indefinite (s 118-145(3)). During this choice, no other dwelling can be treated as your main residence except under the changing-residences overlap (s 118-140) — s 118-145(4). For replacement dwellings after compulsory acquisition/destruction, s 118-147 provides a separate choice with its own 6-year income-use limit (s 118-147(4)).

nodes.label: Are you building, repairing or renovating a dwelling on the land (s 118-150)?
nodes.body: If you have an ownership interest in land (except a life interest) and build a dwelling, or repair/renovate/finish building one, you can choose to treat the dwelling as your main residence from the time you acquired the interest (s 118-150(2)). Conditions: the dwelling becomes your main residence as soon as practicable after work finishes AND continues as your main residence for at least 3 months (s 118-150(3)). The choice operates for the shorter of 4 years (or longer if the Commissioner allows) before it becomes your main residence, and the period from acquisition to when it becomes your main residence (s 118-150(4)). If the individual dies, s 118-155 provides a separate choice for the surviving joint tenant or trustee.

nodes.label: Does the CGT event happen to adjacent land (or adjacent structure) only, without also happening to the dwelling?
nodes.body: If the CGT event happens only to adjacent land (or an adjacent structure) and not also to the dwelling itself, the exemption does NOT apply under the general rule in s 118-165. However, a separate exemption for compulsory acquisitions of adjacent land applies under ss 118-240 to 118-265, subject to the 2-hectare limit (s 118-120(3)/s 118-245(1)(f)) and foreign-resident exclusions (s 118-245(3)).

nodes.label: Full exemption — capital gain/loss disregarded (s 118-110)
nodes.body: The capital gain or loss from the CGT event is disregarded. This is the basic case: you are an individual, the dwelling was your main residence throughout your ownership period, you did not acquire it from a deceased estate, and you are not an excluded foreign resident or a foreign resident failing the life events test. Note: if the dwelling was used for income-producing purposes during any period, s 118-190 may claw back part of the exemption (see partial exemption rules).

nodes.label: Was the dwelling your main residence for only part of the ownership period?
nodes.body: If the dwelling was your main residence for only part of the ownership period, you get only a partial exemption under s 118-185. The formula is: Non-main residence days / Total days in ownership period × capital gain/loss (s 118-185(2)). This section does not apply if the dwelling was acquired from a deceased estate (use ss 118-195/118-200 instead). Also does NOT apply if you are an excluded foreign resident or a foreign resident failing the life events test (s 118-185(3)). The s 118-145 absence choice can reduce the non-main residence days by treating the dwelling as your main residence during the absence.

nodes.label: Partial exemption — only part of the capital gain is disregarded
nodes.body: The exemption is partial under either s 118-185 (non-main residence days formula), s 118-190 (income-producing use adjustment), or both. The combined effect: non-main residence days proportion reduces the exempt portion, and income-producing use during main residence periods increases the assessable portion. Calculate the capital gain/loss under s 118-185 formula, then apply the s 118-190 income-use adjustment. Note: s 118-192 (first income use after August 1996) resets cost base to market value, effectively exempting the pre-income-use gain entirely. The residence may also be treated as a 'taxable use' under Div 118 definitions.

nodes.label: Deceased estate rules (ss 118-195 to 118-210)
nodes.body: Special rules apply when the dwelling was acquired from a deceased estate (by a beneficiary or trustee). The full exemption under s 118-195 requires the deceased to have acquired the interest on or after 20 Sep 1985 AND the dwelling was the deceased's main residence just before death AND was not then used for income — plus the beneficiary's interest ends within 2 years of death (or longer if Commissioner allows). OR the deceased acquired the interest before 20 Sep 1985 AND the dwelling was, from death until ownership ends, the main residence of the spouse, a person with a right to occupy under the will, or the beneficiary (s 118-195 table). If s 118-195 does NOT apply, a partial exemption applies under s 118-200. The deceased must not have been an excluded foreign resident just before death (s 118-195(1)(c)). Trustee rules under s 118-210 apply where a trustee acquires a dwelling under a will for occupation by an individual.

nodes.label: Does the dwelling qualify for the full deceased estate exemption (s 118-195)?
nodes.body: The table in s 118-195(1) has two items. Item 1: deceased acquired interest on/after 20 Sep 1985 + dwelling was deceased's main residence just before death + not then used for income + your interest ends within 2 years of death (or longer allowed by Commissioner). Item 2: deceased acquired interest before 20 Sep 1985 + from death until your interest ends, the dwelling was the main residence of (a) the spouse just before death, (b) a person with right to occupy under the will, or (c) the beneficiary who brought about the CGT event. The deceased must not have been an excluded foreign resident just before death (s 118-195(1)(c)). Note: If just before death the deceased was an excluded foreign resident, disregard paras (a) and (b) in column 3 of item 2, and disregard para (c) if the individual is an excluded foreign resident at the time of the CGT event (s 118-195(1A)).

nodes.label: Calculate partial exemption for deceased estate dwelling (s 118-200)
nodes.body: If s 118-195 does not apply, you calculate the capital gain/loss using the formula in s 118-200(2): Non-main residence days / Total days × capital gain/loss. 'Non-main residence days' includes: (a) days in deceased's ownership period when the dwelling was not the deceased's main residence; (aa) if deceased was an excluded foreign resident just before death — all remaining days in the deceased's ownership period; and (b) days from death until your interest ends when the dwelling was not the main residence of the s 118-195 table individuals. Option: ignore post-death days if your interest ends within 2 years of death and the deceased was not an excluded foreign resident (s 118-200(3)). If the dwelling was the deceased's main residence just before death and not then used for income, ignore pre-death non-main residence days (s 118-200(4)). Adjustments for multiple inheritances apply under s 118-205.

nodes.label: Trustee acquiring dwelling under will (s 118-210)
nodes.body: If you are the trustee of a deceased estate and, under the will, acquire a dwelling for occupation by an individual: (1) if the CGT event happens in relation to the individual and you receive no money/property — the gain is disregarded, the individual inherits the trustee's cost base and acquisition time (s 118-210(2)); (2) if you receive money/property or the event involves another entity and the dwelling was the individual's main residence throughout — no gain/loss (s 118-210(3)); (3) if it was the individual's main residence for only part of the period — partial exemption using the non-main residence days formula (s 118-210(4)). Only specified CGT events apply (s 118-210(5)). Does not apply if the deceased was an excluded foreign resident just before death (s 118-210(6)).

nodes.label: Spouse transfer interaction (ss 118-178/118-180 and s 118-170)
nodes.body: Two key interactions: (1) ss 118-178/118-180 (carry-over of main residence history on a marriage breakdown roll-over under Subdivision 126-A) — the transferee spouse steps into the transferor's shoes for ownership period and main residence use; (2) s 118-170 (spouses with different main residences) — where you and your spouse have different main residences during a period, you must either choose one dwelling as the main residence of both, or nominate different dwellings (splitting the exemption proportionally based on ownership interests). Section 118-175 provides a similar rule for dependent children.

nodes.label: Carry-over of ownership and use under s 118-178 (spouse transfer)
nodes.body: If you acquired the dwelling from a former partner under a Subdivision 126-A roll-over (marriage breakdown), the main residence exemption applies as if: (a) your ownership interest commenced when your former partner's commenced; (b) from that time until the former partner's interest ended, you used the dwelling the same way they did; and (c) it was your main residence for the same number of days it was theirs (s 118-178(2)). This carries the transferor's period of ownership and use forward to the transferee. Section 118-180 provides a more limited rule for acquisitions from a company or trust — you are treated as owning the dwelling during the period the entity owned it, but it cannot be treated as your main residence during that period (s 118-180(2)).

nodes.label: Do you and your spouse have different main residences?
nodes.body: If during a period your dwelling is your main residence and another dwelling is your spouse's main residence (except a spouse living permanently separately from you), you must EITHER choose one dwelling as the main residence of both (s 118-170(1)(a)) OR nominate different dwellings (s 118-170(1)(b)). If you nominate different dwellings, the exemption is split: if your interest in the dwelling you chose is not more than half of total interests, it is taken to be your main residence for the whole period; otherwise, it is taken to be your main residence for half the period (s 118-170(2)-(4)). A similar choice rule applies for dependent children under 18 (s 118-175).

nodes.label: Special disability trust rules (ss 118-215 to 118-230)
nodes.body: Special disability trust rules (ss 118-215 to 118-230) extend the main residence exemption to dwellings owned by a special disability trust (or its trustee) used as the main residence of the principal beneficiary. These rules apply independently of the deceased-estate regime — they are an extension of the exemption under s 118-105, not a sub-branch of ss 118-195 to 118-210.

nodes.label: Compulsory acquisition of adjacent land only (ss 118-240 to 118-265)
nodes.body: A separate exemption for compulsory acquisitions of adjacent land (but not the dwelling itself) applies under ss 118-240 to 118-265. The exemption applies if the CGT event involves compulsory acquisition or similar arrangements (s 118-250). The total adjacent land area is limited to 2 hectares (s 118-245(1)(f)). If the area exceeds 2 hectares, you can choose a partial exemption for land within the maximum exempt area (s 118-245(2)). Partial exemption rules under s 118-260 may increase the gain/loss by a reasonable amount considering non-main residence use and income-producing use. The maximum exempt area is reduced by any earlier exempt disposals of adjacent land (s 118-255). Section 118-265 extends these rules to adjacent structures of flats/home units. Does NOT apply if you are an excluded foreign resident or a foreign resident failing the life events test (s 118-245(3)).

nodes.label: Main residence CGT position determined — exemption applied (full or partial) or denied
nodes.body: The Subdivision 118-B main residence exemption analysis is complete. The outcome depends on: whether the dwelling was your main residence throughout (full exemption), for only part of the period (partial exemption under s 118-185), with income-producing use (adjustment under s 118-190), and whether the foreign-resident boundary blocks the exemption entirely (s 118-110(3)-(5)). Deceased estate dwellers have their own rules (full under s 118-195 or partial under s 118-200). Spouse transfers may carry over ownership/use history (ss 118-178/118-180). Compulsory acquisitions of adjacent land have separate treatment (ss 118-245/118-260). Special disability trusts have their own regime (ss 118-215 to 118-230). Cross-references: Div 855 (foreign resident CGT) and Subdiv 126-A (marriage breakdown roll-over) may be relevant.

nodes.label: No exemption available — normal CGT rules apply
nodes.body: If the dwelling was not your main residence (and no extension rule applies), or you are not an individual, or the CGT event is not covered, or the dwelling definition is not satisfied, the main residence exemption does not apply. The capital gain is assessable under normal CGT rules (Division 100+).
